previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with severe right ankle pain and swelling, initially concerning for septic arthritis. Arthrocentesis revealed purulent fluid with over 400,000 WBCs and monosodium urate crystals, leading to a diagnosis of gout. Blood and synovial fluid cultures were negative, supporting gout over infection. She was treated with a short course of IV antibiotics, which were discontinued after 48 hours due to clinical improvement and negative cultures. Treatment included prednisone, colchicine, and acetaminophen, with morphine for breakthrough pain. She experienced an asymptomatic episode of hypotension on hospital day 2, managed with fluid bolus and temporary hold of antihypertensives. Her GERD symptoms resolved with continued protonix. She improved steadily, with reduced pain, swelling, and inflammation markers, and was discharged to extended care with plans to start allopurinol after flare resolution and podiatry follow-up for heel pain.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Upper GI bleed - Patient had history of spitting up dark 
flecks suggestive of  coffee ground emesis. She was admitted to 
the floor where serial HCt were checked and remained stable 
except for one slight drop from 37.1 -> 33.2 on ___. After this 
drop her HCt remained between 33.2 - 35.0.  She did not have any 
guiac positive stools during the admission. She had one 
additional episode of emisis which she reported had a few small 
black flecks, but had no frank hematemesis. She was started on 
IV BID PPI. During this admission, after being cleared by 
cardiology, she had an endoscopic study which showed mild 
erosions in the esophagus that according to the GI fellow could 
have been a source of some mild bleeding. She was also noted to 
have a large intrathoracic stomach secondary to a hiatal hernia. 
 She also had a barium swallow study which showed the hiatal 
hernia but did not give any other information regarding possible 
source of bleeding. 
.
# Abdominal pain - during admission, the patinet complained of 
intermittend LUQ/L flank pain. She had a CT scan which again 
demonstrated a large hiatal hernia and diverticulosis. We 
believe that her abdominal pain is likely due to her hernia. In 
addition, she had several hypodense lesions on her L kidney 
which were most likely cysts but in the setting of prior Breast 
CA need to be followed up by her PCP and oncologist.  Before D/C 
a UA was checked which showed mild microscopic hematuria which 
was attributed to the foley catheter.  Of note, her prior UA 
from this admission had no red cells in it.  She should have a 
repeat UA at her PCP's office to confirm that she does not have 
continued hematuria. Should she develop further hematuria in the 
future, she will need more extensive urologic work up. 
.
# Hiatal hernia - Pt with history of hernia, now with worsening 
symptoms secondary (regurgitation, shortness of breath, 
abdominal pain) to hernia, so evaluated by surgery during this 
admission.  Patient will follow up with Dr ___ as 
anoutpatient for elective repair of her hernia if appropriate 
after full cardiac workup and any additional medical 
optimization has been completed. At time of discharge, patient 
is able to tolerate POs w/out vomiting.
.
# Cardiac - During this admission, cardiology was consulted for 
the patient's report of chest pain and DOE as an outpatient. 
Cardiology recommended inpatient ECHO, which was performed and 
was unremarkable. In addition, cardiology recommeds a repeat 
outpatient stress test pre-operatively and for the patient to 
re-start ASA at some point when thought safe from a GI 
standpoint (and is not ___, as well as to start on a 
low-dose B-blocker, which can be considered by her outpatient 
cardiologist with whom she has an appointment the day after d/c. 

.
# Gout - The patient was continued on colchicine during this 
admission with no further gout flares.
.
# Acute Renal Failure - The patient had acute renal failure 
during this admission with a Cr rising to 1.5 before returning 
to the patient's baseline.  This was in the setting of 
post-contrast enhanced CT scan upon admission, as well as 
decreased PO intake and was likely primarily pre-renal. Upon 
instituting a regular diet, her renal failure resolved. Of note, 
the patient did also have small hypodense lesions on her L 
kidney noted on her CT scan report which should be followed up 
by her PCP ___ oncologist as an outpatient. She also had an 
episode of microscopic hematuria upon foley d/c which should be 
followed up as an outpatient.
.
# Hypokalemia - The patient had hypokalemia with a K+ to 2.9 
during this admission. This resolved with oral potassium and 1 
dose of IV potassium therapy. She will be re-started on her home 
potassium upon discharge and should have electrolytes re-checked 
as an outpatient. 
.
# Thrombocytopenia - During this admission, the patient had 
thrombocytopenia which appears to be stable and chronic.  She 
was seen by heme/onc while inpatient and will follow up with her 
outpatient hematologist in the next few weeks. 
.
# Hypertension - Her blood pressure was well-controlled during 
this admission. Blood pressure medicines were held one day b/c 
of systolic BP in the high 90's. On the day of discharge, her BP 
os 116/80.

# Osteopenia - Alendronate held b/c of assoc with GI irritation.
